# Analysis

## Geometric limits

> [!theorem] Geometric limit
> If |q|<1, then q^n tends to zero.

^geometric

## Eventual comparison

> [!theorem] Sandwich
> If a_n <= b_n <= c_n for every n >= N and both bounding sequences tend to L, then b_n tends to L. A finite initial set of indices does not affect convergence.

^sandwich

## Positive sequence monotonicity

> [!proposition] Quotient criterion
> For positive terms, comparing v_(k+1)/v_k with 1 determines increase or decrease.

^quotient

## Limit operations

> [!proposition] Sum and product
> Sums and products of convergent sequences converge to the sums and products of their limits. Also 1/(n+1) tends to zero.

^operations

## Derivatives

Derivative vocabulary ^derivative-title

The class C^2 means that two derivatives exist and are continuous. The derivative of x^2 is 2x. The preceding derivative-title anchor belongs only to the title paragraph, not this paragraph.

## Local remainder bounds

> [!definition] Big O
> r(x)=O(x^2) as x approaches zero from the right means there are M, delta > 0 such that |r(x)| <= M x^2 for all 0 < x <= delta, with one common M.

^big-o

> [!theorem] Taylor
> If f is C^2 on [0,1] and f(0)=0, Taylor-Young yields f(x)=f'(0)x+O(x^2) as x approaches zero from the right.

^taylor

## Arithmetic sum

> [!proposition] Sum
> The sum of k from 1 to n equals n(n+1)/2.

^sum

# Solutions

%% clew:unit correction corr-1 %%

## Correction 1

Correction ^corr-1

> [!reponse] Answer 1
> Since |2/5|<1, u_n tends to zero.
> [Question](../Exercise-sheet/sheet.md#^q-1)

^r-1

> [!reponse] Answer 2
> v_n=2-1/(n+1), so v_n tends to 2.
> [Question](../Exercise-sheet/sheet.md#^q-2)

^r-2

> [!reponse] Answer 3
> h'(x)=-2x.
> [Question](../Exercise-sheet/sheet.md#^q-3)

^r-3

> [!reponse] Answer 4
> Taylor-Young gives f(x)=f'(0)x+O(x^2). Write f(k/n^2)=f'(0)k/n^2+r_(n,k), with |r_(n,k)|<=M_k/n^2. Sum the linear part to obtain f'(0)(n+1)/(2n); the sum of remainders tends to zero, so the limit is f'(0)/2.
> [Question](../Exercise-sheet/sheet.md#^q-4)

^r-4

> [!reponse] Answer 5
> For a fixed n, the positive binomial coefficients have ratio (n-k)/(k+1), increasing to the middle and decreasing symmetrically. Separate the two endpoint terms 1 and the two next terms 1/n. The remaining n-3 terms are at most 2/(n(n-1)), so 2<=z_n<=2+2/n+2(n-3)/(n(n-1)). The sandwich gives limit 2.
> [Question](../Exercise-sheet/sheet.md#^q-5)

^r-5

[Exercise](../Exercise-sheet/sheet.md#^ex-1)
